svg.title: A 13-year-old is seen in urgent care. Nurse's notes: new GI symptoms started 2 days ago with poor appetite and nausea, now with fever, vomiting and occasional diarrhea. He went to bed early last night and showed no interest in video games. His parents are divorced, and the parent worries he eats mostly fast food (especially hamburgers) on weekends. Dark urine was noted in the toilet this morning. Temperature 103.2°F (39.6°C). He says he is very tired and wants to go home to bed. Select three findings that are of immediate concern to the nurse.
svg.desc: Vomiting and a high fever put him at risk for dehydration and electrolyte imbalance, and dark urine may mean a raised bilirubin from liver inflammation. The diarrhea is only occasional, fatigue is expected with his GI illness, and diet and family situation can be addressed later.
